claims.text: A controlled population of coherent ordered B2 nanoprecipitates in a continuous disordered BCC Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr matrix will simultaneously improve room-temperature yield strength and ductility.
The proposed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr microstructure will mitigate density limitations relative to W-based RHEAs.
Equiatomic or near-equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr can initially form either a single disordered BCC phase or a coarse BCC+B2 microstructure with a continuous B2 matrix.
The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has high density.
A continuous B2 matrix or coarse BCC+B2 structure in RHEAs is associated with poor room-temperature ductility.
Controlled aging or severe plastic deformation followed by annealing can produce discrete coherent B2 nanoprecipitates in a continuous BCC Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr matrix.
Aging between 800°C and 1200°C is an appropriate processing window for generating the proposed coherent precipitate morphology.
Precise cooling-rate control is necessary to retain coherent interfaces and prevent precipitate coarsening or continuous phase separation.
Brittle intermetallics and oxide inclusions such as TiO must be avoided to preserve ductility.
Coherent SCCP interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Dislocations will shear or transmit through the B2 precipitates rather than bow around them or initiate cracks at incoherent interfaces.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations that would otherwise promote premature crack initiation.
The inverted BCC+B2 morphology can improve ductility without sacrificing solid-solution and precipitation strengthening.
The processed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will achieve yield strength above 1.0 GPa and tensile elongation above 10% at room temperature.
The proposed alloy will have density below 10 g/cm³.
The proposed alloy will maintain high strength at temperatures of approximately 800°C or above.
A continuous ordered B2 phase acts as a crack path and causes brittle room-temperature failure in conventional Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEAs.
Ductility will degrade if the B2 precipitates coarsen, lose coherency, or form a continuous network.
The approach is bounded by elemental solubility in the BCC matrix and by B2 thermodynamic stability at the processing temperature.
Long-term aging of Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr may produce brittle topologically close-packed phases.
